"You're right, and that's the better version. A pre-check only narrows the race; the conditional write closes it. I'd still keep the stored facts, but their job changes: they become the expected version or idempotency key you hand to the effect call, and the audit trail of why the job thought it was allowed. Where the target system offers no conditional write, I'd at least make the effect idempotent so a lost race costs a duplicate check, not a duplicate charge. Have you seen many APIs where you had to fake the atomic precondition yourself?" [ceec9938]
